note: Pskov, as a junior partner and later dependency of Novgorod, shared in Novgorod's indirect relationship with the Golden Horde — paying tribute through Novgorod's collection mechanism rather than directly. Pskov's position on the western frontier (adjacent to the Teutonic/Livonian Order and Lithuania) meant its military concerns were primarily western, while the Mongol fiscal relationship was mediated through Novgorod. When Moscow absorbed Novgorod (1478), Pskov's Mongol-tributary relationship ended; Pskov was then absorbed by Vasili III (1510) through the same administrative consolidation that had ended Novgorodian independence.

_quarry.structural_significance: Pskov's indirect Horde relationship demonstrates how the Mongol tributary system operated through intermediaries; Pskov's eventual absorption completes the elimination of the last northwestern Russian republican city-states; the pattern of small republics surviving as long as the Mongol tributary system required intermediaries, then falling when Moscow no longer needed them, is politically revealing
